comparison.note: one process, one genesis backend, the same master seed and perturbation; the only difference between the two rows is where the graph operands live

fingerprint.rule: sha256 over seeds + returns + fitness rounded to 6 decimals

parity.note: both residencies run the same graphs on the same values in the same order; only the location of the operands differs, so every field is expected to be bit-identical. A nonzero entry means the two sides handed the graphs different inputs: check sides.*.state_read_parity (Go2 reads the state through the entity getters on the numpy side and through the live solver buffers on the device side) before blaming a graph

throughput.note: median and spread over the timed generations of this process; the warm-up generation is excluded everywhere (it carries the first-step JIT of the compiled kernels and the empty caches)

device.generation_total_scope: generation_total is env.evaluate end to end (host seed draw + reset + steps + run_fitness) measured by the harness; measurements.generations[*].wall_time_s is the environment's own counter, which starts after the host seed draw and stops before run_fitness
device.graph_build_note: per-graph build time is measured inside ExecutableCache.get while the env is constructed; the env builds every executable in __init__, so this table is the compile cost and every later generation is a cache hit
device.sync_note: common.sync() runs before and after every generation; it calls torch.cuda.synchronize() only when a HIP/CUDA device is available (it reported True here) and is a no-op on a CPU-resident run, where every timed region is host wall clock (time.perf_counter anyway)

phases.note: one row per residency; the two environments are built one after the other in this process

numpy.generation_total_scope: generation_total is env.evaluate end to end (host seed draw + reset + steps + run_fitness) measured by the harness; measurements.generations[*].wall_time_s is the environment's own counter, which starts after the host seed draw and stops before run_fitness
numpy.graph_build_note: per-graph build time is measured inside ExecutableCache.get while the env is constructed; the env builds every executable in __init__, so this table is the compile cost and every later generation is a cache hit
numpy.sync_note: common.sync() runs before and after every generation; it calls torch.cuda.synchronize() only when a HIP/CUDA device is available (it reported True here) and is a no-op on a CPU-resident run, where every timed region is host wall clock (time.perf_counter anyway)

timings.note: process totals; per-generation breakdowns live in measurements.sides[*].generations
